skill.name: geo-database
skill.description: Access NCBI GEO for public gene expression and genomics data. Search, retrieve, download, parse, and analyze GEO datasets, samples, platforms, and profiles.
skill.summary: Search, retrieve, and analyze public NCBI GEO gene expression datasets.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The skill is primarily documentation and examples for public NCBI GEO data access. Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, official public URLs, placeholder keys, dictionary key access, and genomics identifiers. The FTP references are confirmed medium-risk because they recommend unauthenticated transport and recursive downloads that can affect data integrity and local resources.

remediation.issue: FTP download guidance uses unauthenticated transport.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer HTTPS or GEOparse downloads when available, and add checksum or size validation before processing files.

remediation.issue: Recursive bulk download examples can consume large disk space.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit limits, expected size checks, and confirmation prompts before using recursive downloads or supplementary directories.

remediation.issue: The API key example shows an inline placeholder assignment.
remediation.suggestion: Show loading the NCBI API key from an environment variable or local secret manager instead of inline assignment.

content.value_statement: Public GEO datasets are hard to search, download, and prepare consistently. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through NCBI GEO search, retrieval, and transcriptomics analysis workflows.
actual_capabilities: Search GEO DataSets and GEO Profiles with Biopython Entrez examples.
Retrieve GSE, GSM, GPL, GDS, and profile metadata.
Download GEO series matrix, SOFT, MINiML, and supplementary files.
Use GEOparse to parse series, samples, platforms, and expression tables.
Prepare quality control, differential expression, clustering, and meta-analysis workflows.
Reference GEO FTP layouts, E-utilities endpoints, and common file formats.
limitations: Requires internet access to NCBI and related public documentation sites.
Does not verify dataset biological quality or clinical suitability.
Large GEO files can require significant storage and download time.
Examples need a valid user email and optional NCBI API key configuration.

use_cases.title: Find expression studies
use_cases.description: Search GEO for studies by disease, organism, platform, publication date, or accession.

use_cases.title: Prepare analysis datasets
use_cases.description: Download GEO series files and convert them into expression matrices with sample metadata.

use_cases.title: Compare public cohorts
use_cases.description: Plan quality control, differential expression, clustering, and meta-analysis across GEO studies.

prompt_templates.title: Search for studies
prompt_templates.prompt: Find public GEO studies about human breast cancer RNA-seq. Return useful search terms, likely accessions, and filters to review.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize a series
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the GEO workflow to inspect GSE123456. Summarize the study design, sample groups, platform, and available files.

prompt_templates.title: Plan data extraction
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a safe plan to download a GEO series matrix and parse expression values with GEOparse. Include rate limits and storage checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design a meta-analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare several GEO studies for TP53 expression. Plan accession selection, platform mapping, normalization checks, batch effect review, and result validation.

output_examples.input: Search for human diabetes expression profiling studies.
output_examples.output: A ranked shortlist of GEO studies, search filters, organism constraints, platform notes, and next review steps.

output_examples.input: Summarize one GEO series before download.
output_examples.output: A concise study summary with sample counts, experimental groups, platform accessions, file types, and quality concerns.

output_examples.input: Plan differential expression analysis from a GEO matrix.
output_examples.output: A workflow covering data download, metadata review, group assignment, normalization checks, statistical testing, and citation reminders.

best_practices: Set Entrez.email and respect NCBI rate limits before running batch queries.
Prefer HTTPS or official library downloads when available, and verify large downloads before analysis.
Check sample metadata, platform annotation, and normalization before comparing expression values.
anti_patterns: Hard-code real NCBI API keys in shared notebooks or scripts.
Run recursive bulk downloads without storage limits or a file plan.
Compare studies without checking batch effects, platform differences, or processing methods.

faq.question: What databases does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on NCBI GEO DataSets, GEO Profiles, series, samples, platforms, and related GEO file formats.

faq.question: Can it download raw and processed files?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains GEOparse, E-utilities, series matrix files, SOFT files, MINiML files, and supplementary downloads.

faq.question: Does it perform statistical analysis automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow examples for quality control, differential expression, clustering, and meta-analysis.

faq.question: Do I need an NCBI API key?
faq.answer: No. An API key is optional, but it can increase E-utilities rate limits when configured securely.

faq.question: Is this suitable for clinical decisions?
faq.answer: No. GEO data and example analyses need independent scientific and clinical validation before use.

faq.question: What should I check before downloading data?
faq.answer: Review expected file sizes, storage capacity, sample metadata, platform annotation, and NCBI usage guidelines.
